verification_candidates.claim_text: Large studies link acetaminophen use in pregnancy to autism in children.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: large studies linking that medication to autism in children
verification_candidates.rationale: The existence and direction of a link between prenatal acetaminophen and autism can be checked against the epidemiological literature.

verification_candidates.claim_text: The Harvard School of Public Health dean believes the association between acetaminophen in pregnancy and autism is causal.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: the Harvard School of Public Health dean. Has made a very conclusive statement that he believes the association is causal
verification_candidates.rationale: Whether a Harvard dean made such a statement can be verified.

verification_candidates.claim_text: The duration of acetaminophen use in pregnancy is associated with the risk of autism in children.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: associations. Between the duration of acetaminophen use and the risk of autism in children subsequently
verification_candidates.rationale: A duration-response association is a checkable epidemiological claim.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Acetaminophen use near the time of birth is associated with the risk of autism in children.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: there are associations. Between the duration of acetaminophen use and the risk of autism in children subsequently, as well as the proximity to the time of birth
verification_candidates.rationale: The claim that birth-proximity exposure is associated with autism risk can be checked.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Acetaminophen levels in newborn cord blood are associated with the degree of autism risk.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: acetaminophen that's shown up in the cord blood of newborn babies, and that cord blood level has been associated with the degree of risk
verification_candidates.rationale: A cord-blood level association is a checkable biomarker claim.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Autism has increased 400 percent in recent decades.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: We have an epidemic of autism that has increased 400 percent
verification_candidates.rationale: The 400 percent increase can be checked against autism surveillance data.

verification_candidates.claim_text: There is no known cause of autism.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: we don't have a known cause
verification_candidates.rationale: The claim that autism has no known cause is checkable against current scientific consensus.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Acetaminophen in pregnancy may be a cause of autism.
verification_candidates.rationale: This is the central causal claim behind the FDA announcement and should be checked against the evidence.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Leucovorin is a treatment for autism.
verification_candidates.rationale: Whether leucovorin treats autism is checkable against clinical evidence.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Some children with autism have an autoimmune disease.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: some kids with autism actually have an autoimmune disease
verification_candidates.rationale: The autoimmune subset claim can be checked against studies of folate receptor antibodies in autism.

verification_candidates.claim_text: The mechanism may be that the body creates antibodies that block folate receptors on the brain, restricting folate from entering the brain.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: The mechanism may be that the body is creating antibodies that block the folate receptors on their brain
verification_candidates.rationale: The folate-receptor antibody mechanism is a checkable scientific claim.
